page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.8-32 is a flexible compute instance powered by the AMD EPYC 7J13 processor running at 2.55 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs via multithreading, alongside 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 64 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache per core cluster. Hardware cryptographic acceleration is enabled via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, accompanied by standard AVX vector execution, though AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

Benchmark measurements reveal strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng recording 2686.48, placing it within the top 25 percent of tracked instances. Multi-core compute performance aligns with mid-range expectations, achieving 21426.44 in stress-ng and 10087.0 in Geekbench multi-core. In memory throughput tests, the instance records 86.89 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB reads and 43.72 GB/sec in writes. Execution speeds in application benchmarks include 15.34 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 15.37 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The instance does not bundle local NVMe storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, necessitating external block volumes for persistent data retention. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio establishes strong computational density per gigabyte of RAM, offering favorable cost efficiency for compute-centric workloads that do not demand extensive memory allocations. Best-fit use cases include software compilation, web serving, CI/CD runners, batch processing, and microservice application deployments.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.8-32 is a compute-focused instance utilizing an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor at 2.55 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 physical cores, 16 vCPUs, and 32.0 GB of RAM, offering an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance incorporates 16 MB of L3 cache, cryptographic support through AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, and AVX instruction sets. Benchmark evaluations show upper-tier single-core compute capability, reaching 2686.48 in stress-ng, while multi-core compute registers 21426.44 and Geekbench multi-core achieves 10087.0. Large-block memory bandwidth delivers 86.89 GB/sec read and 43.72 GB/sec write rates. With no bundled local storage or GPUs, this instance relies on network volumes and achieves high cost efficiency for compute-dense workloads. It is well matched for software compilation, web servers, API tiers, and general-purpose batch processing jobs.
